text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English author HENRY FIELDING who wrote the famous novel "Tom Jones" was born in 1707.

One this century's most important politicians was born in 1870. VLADIMIR ILICH LENIN one of the founders of the Russian Communist Party, became leader of the Bolshevik Party in the Russian parliament, and inspired the Russian Revolution. He became the first Communist leader of Russia, and was widely revered by Communists all around the world up until the fall of
the Soviet Union.
American scientist ROBERT OPPENHEIMER was born in 1904. Credited as being the man who invented the atomic bomb, he became an anti-nuclear activist after seeing the A-bomb used on Japan.
DAPHNE AKHURST, the first Australian woman to play at Wimbledon, was born in 1903.
Noted Australian artist SIR SYDNEY NOLAN was born in 1917. He became internationally famous for a series of paintings about NED KELLY.

Australian businessman ALAN BOND was born in 1938. Originally a signpainter he made his fortune through real estate development, then lost it through over-borrowing during the 1980's. The highpoint of his career was in 1983 when his yacht "Australia 2" won the America's Cup.

British guitarist, singer and songwriter PETER FRAMPTON was born in 1950. In 1971 he became a solo performer after being instrumental in the formation of several earlier bands. His supposed farewell double-album "FRAMPTON COMES ALIVE" was a bestseller. Hits included "Show Me The Way" and "I'm In You" (1977).
** EVENTS **
1348 : The Duchess of Salisbury lost her garter while

dancing with King EDWARD THE FOURTH of England. He picked the garter up and attached it to his own leg. The King later marked the occasion by creating the Order of the Knight of the Garter, which is England's highest order of knighthood.
1793 : U.S. President GEORGE WASHINGTON issued a
Proclamation of Neutrality to ensure that the United States did not become involved in the war between France and Britain.
1834 : The Quadruple Alliance was formed between Britain,
France, Portugal and Spain, supporting ISABELLA II's claim to the Spanish throne against Don CARLOS.
1838 : The British steamship Sirius became the first to
cross the Atlantic from Britain to New York on steam power only. The journey from Cork to New York took 18 days 10 hours.
1876 : The National Baseball League was formed in the US.
1889 : The famous Oaklahoma land run began. Would-be

settlers raced into the territory to claim an area as their own. Each successful claimant received 160 acres of prairie. The land run created a number of fortunes, and later inspired the musical Oaklahoma.
1915 : The second battle of Ypres started when German
troops released clouds of deadly chlorine gas on British troops; it was the first major gas attack of World War One.
1944 : Allied forces landed at Hollandia in Dutch New
Guinea in World War Two.
1945 : General MacARTHUR announced that Cebu Island's
capture had ended the Central Philippines campaign.
1947 : The photo-finish camera was used for the first
time at Epsom in the UK.
1954 : Russia broke off diplomatic relations with

Australian over the Petrov affair. Soviet Embassy official, VLADIMIR PETROV defected weeks before he was to return to Moscow. PETROV, who was also an officer in the organisation controlling the Soviet secret police (KGB), gave Australian authorities evidence of Soviet spying activities. Northern Territory police stopped two Soviet couriers escorting Mrs PETROV to a plane in Darwin. She too was offered politicial asylum and after finding her husband was still alive she decided to stay.
1959 : Angler ALF DEAN landed a 5.3 metre, 1208 kg White
Pointer Shark near Ceduna in South Australia. It was the largest shark ever caught with a fishing rod.
1969 : British lone yachtsman ROBIN KNOX-JOHNSTON arrived
at Falmouth after completing the first solo non-stop circumnavigation of the Earth in just 312 days.
1971 : Haiti's hated dictator PAPA DOC DUVALIER died

peacefully in bed at the age of 63. His 14 year reign saw thousands of people butchered by his henchmen, the so-called Tonton Macoute. PAPA DOC survived six assassination attempts, liked to use chicken entrails to read the future, and keep the heads of decapitated rivals.
1972 : Two young rowers landed safely on Queensland's
Hayman Island after leaving San Francisco almost a year earlier. They were last sighted off the Solomon Islands eight weeks earlier. At one stage they were feared lost in one of two
cyclones that swept through the area. The two Pacific rowers were JOHN FAIRFAX and SYLVIA COOK.
1983 : The Federal Government expelled VALERIY IVANOV,
from the Russian embassy in Canberra, for spying. The expulsion started the "Ivanov Affair" which virtually destroyed former Labor Party National Secretary DAVID COOMBE.
1984 : French and US scientists claimed they had isolated

the virus that causes AIDS. Announcing the discovery of the AIDS virus the US Health and Human Services Secretary, MARGARET HECKLER, said she hoped that blood test would be available in six months and a vaccine ready in two years. In the US, ROBERT GALLO of the National Cancer Institute, named the virus HHTLV-III, while the Pasteur Institute in Paris called the virus LAV. It is commonly known as HIV.
1994 : Former U.S. president RICHARD NIXON died aged 81.
He was the 37th President of the United States from 1969 until his resignation in 1974 amid the Watergate scandal.
1995 : The Tutsi-dominated Rwandan army opened fire on
Hutu refugees in the Kibeho refugee camp; death toll reports varied from 300 to 2000.
